idea-plugin.name: SSRF Allow-List Bypass Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags an outbound HTTP call (new URL(...), RestTemplate.getForObject/postForObject/exchange/ getForEntity) using an endpoint parameter that was only validated with .startsWith(...)/ .contains(...) against a raw URL string -- structurally bypassable regardless of the specific allow-listed literal (CWE-918). Confirmed real via CVE-2024-22243 (Spring Framework, 2024): a regex mismatch in UriComponentsBuilder let https://evil.com[@127.0.0.1 pass exactly this kind of check while a real URL parser resolves a different host.

Uses a real, hand-written URL/URI parser (this catalog's SIXTH full grammar) to confirm the validation literal really is URL/host-shaped -- and requires the specific validate-then-use CONTROL-FLOW shape (not just taint reaching an HTTP sink, which CodeQL's generic Java SSRF query already covers) to stay precise and avoid duplicating that broader rule.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only a bare (non-concatenated) tainted `String` parameter; only `.startsWith`/`.contains` as the recognized validation; the sink must be in the same `if`'s `then` branch. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Endpoint parameter validated only with startsWith/contains before an outbound HTTP call
